build an rpg and farming simulator: Farming & Animal Husbandry

​Crops: Planting, watering, and harvesting seasonal crops (e.g., strawberries in Spring, blueberries in Summer, pumpkins in Fall).

​Livestock: Raising chickens, ducks, cows, goats, and pigs. Animals produce goods that can be converted into artisan products (like turning milk into cheese or truffles into truffle oil).

​Farm Types: At the start, you choose a farm layout tailored to different playstyles-from classic agricultural plots to riverland fishing spots or wilderness maps with monsters.

​⛏️ Mining & Combat

​The Mines: A 120-floor subterranean system filled with ores (copper, iron, gold, iridium), gemstones, and hostile monsters.

​Combat: Simple real-time sword and weapon combat used to clear floors, gather crafting materials, and discover deeper underground locations like the Skull Cavern.

​🎣 Fishing & Foraging

​Fishing: A skill-based minigame that changes depending on the weather, season, time of day, and water body (ocean, river, mountain lake).

​Foraging: Gathering wild berries, mushrooms, and trees across the map to craft supplies and fences.

​💬 Social Life & Town Dynamics

​Pelican Town: Home to over 30 unique villagers, each with their own schedules, cutscenes, backstories, and personalities.

​Relationships: You can talk to villagers, give them gifts, participate in seasonal town festivals, and even marry one of the 12 eligible bachelors or bachelorettes.

​Roommates & Family: You can build a home, have children with a spouse, or ask Krobus (a friendly shadow monster) to move in as a roommate.

image_prompt.text: Pelican Town's shop row - general store, blacksmith, and quest-giving villagers clustered so the walk back from the farm is short
Lanes chaining each farm plot to the town, the mine entrance, the beach, and the forage woods
Task stations of the daily loop - tilled planting beds, watering points, animal pens and feed troughs, and artisan machines turning milk into cheese and truffles into oil
Pelican Town as a settlement with no hostile spawns, where players restock, gift villagers, and turn in quests
Villager houses, the shops, and the player's own farmhouse, entered from the street rather than used from outside
Monster clearings on the wilderness farm map and hostile chambers down in the mines, set off the walked routes
A subterranean mine of 120 descending floors under the farm, ore veins and gem clusters thickening with depth, opening into a deeper Skull Cavern
Ocean shoreline, a river through the valley, and a mountain lake, each with its own fishing water
Alternate starting farm layouts - classic tilled acreage, a riverland farm cut by water, a wilderness farm with monster ground
An open square where the seasonal town festivals are held

layout_placement.text: Plant, water, harvest, milk, and process stations that fire the repeatable job loop
Seasonal crops in the beds, ore and gemstones in the mine walls, and wild berries, mushrooms, and timber across the map
Emitter points inside the mine floors and wilderness nests where monsters come from
Interior volumes for the farmhouse, villager homes, and shops
Over 30 villagers placed on daily schedules around the town

notes: Mixed and close: Simulation dominant (farming, animal husbandry, artisan processing - a repeatable job loop), RPG secondary for the town, the mines, and combat. Called for Simulation because the farm is the thing the player returns to.

Shape conflict the file cannot resolve: the personal farm is plot-isolated and the 120-floor mine is world-underground, and both are shapes. Built the farm and carried the mine as free text; a real build of the mine adds P2 + P3.
Preset name Sandbox is a poor label for a farming sim - it was chosen because it is the only Simulation preset carrying isolated per-player plots.
Seasons, weather, fishing minigame, relationships, and marriage are non-spatial and were dropped.

answers.answer: Use a soft storybook countryside look, matching the cozy farming RPG tone.

answers.ask: Is the mine a real 120 floors, or a handful of floors that repeat with depth? 120 built floors is a different build entirely.
answers.answer: Make it a real 120-floor mine, as specified, with floors progressing through the stated ore tiers and deeper areas.

answers.ask: Does each player get their own farm, or does one server share a single farm?
answers.answer: Each player gets their own farm so they can choose and develop their selected farm layout independently.
